text:
lina: reproducible issue on mobile: switching from cellular -> wifi mid-stream sometimes shows duplicated fragments and out-of-order JSON objects, causing sampleapp to crash parsing.

omar: saw this once on Android emulator. chunks arrive with overlapping byte ranges after the TCP re-establish.

kevin: do we still rely on purely delimiter-based framing? sounds like we need sequence numbers.

lina: logs: 
```
recv: chunk seq=? data=\"{\"choices\": [\"...\"]}\n
recv: chunk seq=? data=\"{\"choices\": [\"...\"]}\nparser: json.parse error: Unexpected token { in JSON at position 0
```

tara: full repro: open sampleapp, start streaming long response, toggle airplane mode off/on, let wifi attach, see parse error ~50% of runs.

lina: repro with mitmproxy to delay packets: 
```
mitmproxy --listen-port 8080 --mode regular
# delay 200ms on packet range 200-800 bytes
```

omar: interestingly, Go SDK handles this better; it merges fragments by buffering and attempts to reassemble by delimiter detection, JS SDK tries to parse per-chunk which leads to early parse attempts. parity gap again.

kevin: proposal: 1) add optional integer seq header in event data (X-Stream-Seq or as `id:` in SSE) so clients can reorder safely. 2) fallback: parser should append partials to a buffer and only attempt JSON.parse when delimiter or balanced braces detected.

tara: +1 for seq header. also add a small per-chunk checksum field to detect duplication.

lina: can we do this without breaking older clients? maybe server emits seq only when client sets `Accept: text/event-stream; seq=1` or `X-Stream-Opts: seq=1` in request.

omar: agree — feature flag via header. we'll keep delimiter-based default.

kevin: i'll prototype tolerant parser patch in JS SDK: buffer until braces balanced OR until we see closing `\n\n` delimiter, and ignore empty-heartbeat-only chunks. add integration test that reorders chunks and inserts duplicates.

tara: i'll update sampleapp to show a small visual indicator when reorder detected and allow manual resume. good for demo.

devops-bot: created issue INF-5591: stream-reorder-tolerance and assigned to kevin, tara.

kevin: opening draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-js-sdk/pull/1477  includes buffered-parser + new test harness. cc @lina @omar

lina: can we also capture telemetry `stream_chunk_reorder` with fields `client_os`, `seq_gap`, `duplicate`? we need to measure this before/after rollout.

omar: yes, add non-PII tags. also add rollout plan: sampleapp + SDK patch to staging, enable seq header from staging backend behind feature flag for canary clients.

kevin: unit tests added: reorder-dup, missing-delimiter, heartbeat-only. also added e2e using mitmproxy script.

tara: local runs show sampleapp recovers 90% of the time after parser change. still seeing a small percent of failures when packet loss coincides with TLS renegotiation.

lina: note for ops: mobile networks often do TLS session resume which can cause new socket with same flow; we should consider server-side transient queueing to avoid duplicate emission.

kevin: i'll widen the parser window to 1s to tolerate quick handoffs. will monitor effect via telemetry.

devops-bot: PR #1477 opened. CI queued.

lina: thanks—once CI green let's stage to mobile canary and enable seq header for 10% of traffic. i'll coordinate with eng-runtime on rollout window.

omar: fyi i'll file a short note in docs/devex about streaming caveats and the `X-Stream-Opts: seq=1` header.

kevin: CI passed. PR merged and staged to canary. enabling seq header for 10% traffic at 2026-04-02T10:00:00Z.

tara: closing loop: canary metrics show reorder events dropped from 0.7% to 0.05% on mobile. will leave enabled and broaden rollout. :party_popper:
